title: Crusoe Cloud Pricing: GPU Rates and Costs (2026 Guide)
summary: Crusoe Cloud pricing ranges from $1.50 per GPU-hour for L40S to $9.65 for B200. Find monthly costs and calculate expenses for your workload.
body_markdown:
## Activepieces workflows for GPU spend alerts and shutdowns


### Monitor GPU usage and require approval


It doesn't change what Crusoe Cloud charges per hour, but Activepieces can watch your GPU usage and ask a person before anything is stopped.


It reaches its 747 integrations from one flow, and the MIT-licensed core runs on your own infrastructure or on Activepieces Cloud, so the watching that idle-instance bills depend on doesn't need a new system to host.


### Why generic GPU cost controls fall short


Start with the generic fixes. You should have them in place anyway: budget alerts in the provider console, quotas on how many instances a project can launch, and a shutdown script that runs on a schedule. Each one works until it meets a real team.


Console alerts go to one inbox nobody reads. Quotas cap the count, not the waste. A blunt shutdown script eventually kills a training run that looked idle and was only in a slow evaluation phase.


The gap isn't a missing feature. It's the glue between usage data, the people who own the jobs, and the decision to stop something.


### How the workflow is built


Activepieces flows are built from a trigger, steps and branches, and the free plan allows unlimited flows, so one flow per check costs nothing extra.


Its homepage shows the shape of what you'd build: a trigger at the top, an AI agent step that qualifies the input, a condition that branches, then actions such as posting to Slack or sending email, with the steps joined by vertical lines.


Though the homepage example's a sales-lead flow, not a GPU one, the structure transfers directly: trigger, check, branch, notify. You'd swap the lead trigger for a scheduled poll of your usage data, and the branches for "under threshold" and "over threshold."


### Alerting on Crusoe GPU spend thresholds


On a schedule, the flow polls whatever usage or billing data you can export or reach through an API. It compares that data with a limit you set, and posts to Slack or sends email when the limit is crossed.


The value's routing. The alert can go to the engineer who launched the instance, not a shared billing address, and it can include the instance name and how long it's been running.


Check what usage data Crusoe exposes before you commit to a design, since the flow can only act on data you can actually pull.


### Human approval before stopping idle GPU instances


For idle instances, the flow shouldn't stop anything on its own. It sends the owner a request, using a human-approval step, naming the instance and asking whether to stop it.


Approval triggers the stop; silence or refusal leaves it running and escalates later. That keeps the safety of a person's judgment while removing the chore of remembering to ask.


Nobody has to hire a builder for it, either: Activepieces' built-in chat takes a plain description of the idle-instance check and the approval step, and publishes the flow a builder would otherwise have wired by hand.


What lands in your account is an ordinary live flow, listed beside the others, and its run trace records every step the 02:10 check took, from the usage poll to the owner's reply.


It runs under the same RBAC and audit logs as every other flow, so the next overnight alert can be reconstructed by anyone on the team without a certification to decode it. MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production.


This is bounded help. It trims idle waste and surfaces storage and networking creep earlier. The rate card stays exactly where it was, which is why the comparison with other GPU clouds still comes down to cost per finished job.
